rec.name: Cost Transparency Breakdown Section
rec.status: Built — design fix pending (more spacing under circles)

what.text: A full-width content section (editor label 'CRO | Kostentransparenz', i.e. cost transparency) that explains where the price goes. It has a headline, a short intro line, a row of four circular visuals each with a bold percentage (e.g. 45%) and a short label, and a closing sub-headline with an explanatory paragraph. The screenshot shows only placeholder (lorem ipsum) content, so the real copy and what the circles contain are not specified.

why.text: Showing a clear breakdown of what customers pay for (materials, production, margin and so on) makes the price feel fair and understandable. This reduces price objections and distrust and supports a premium price. Big numbers with short labels are quick to scan, and the closing paragraph adds a rational justification.

how.text: Build as a theme section with a heading, a subheading, and 4 repeatable blocks (circle image or chart, percentage, label), followed by a heading and rich-text paragraph. The ticket is a design-flaw note: the percentage and label under each circle sit too close to the circle, so increase the vertical spacing between the circle and its text (the 'More spacing' annotation in the screenshot). Use a 4-column grid on desktop, and stack or use 2 columns on mobile (mobile layout is not shown, so this is an inference).

items: Per block: circle image or icon, percentage value, label
Spacing between circle and percentage/label (the design fix)
Section background and padding (the screenshot shows grey bands above and below)

dependencies.text: No dependencies are stated. Presumably a theme section with blocks and no app. If the percentages should be product-specific, metafields would be needed (inference). It is unclear whether the circles are images or rendered charts.

items: Add-to-cart rate on pages with the section
Price-related objection rate (survey or support tickets)

images.caption: Final UI in the theme editor: heading, intro line, four circles with 45% and a label, and a closing text block. The red annotation 'More spacing' points to the gap between a circle and its percentage.
The 'More spacing' annotation marks the design fix: add space between the circle and its percentage/label.
